rows.result: no build trims in free flight. Mass 1160-1434 g (WL 29-48 N/m2). Low-AR builds sink 1.0-1.3 m/s at the envelope's top (motor current, motor voltage, gear or twist-servo torque); high-AR builds come closest, AR 5.5 sinking 0.25 m/s at 14.7 m/s and 118 W, but at WL 48 stall at about 9 m/s. M2 on the 2S pack would last 7.5-8.4 min at the 106-120 W these free flights draw.

rows.tag: why the small birds fail: fixed mass
rows.numbers: grouped BOM (g), closest Falco AR 5.5 / closest Falco AR 3.5 / Columba AR 3.5 / Larus v20: drive linkage and gearbox plates 317 / 283 / 289 / 326; gears 285 / 193 / 193 / 371; servos 123 each (4 x MKS HV6160); battery 104 each; avionics 38 each; motor 81 / 81 / 81 / 140; wing and tail 86 / 102 / 69 / 166; airframe 91 / 138 / 111 / 122; margin 169 / 159 / 151 / 208; total 1292 / 1220 / 1158 / 1598. The rated drive, the servos the 2S pack can feed and the avionics do not scale with the wing.

items: Falco's drive linkage, plates and airframe still carry the Larus base's dimensions (about 280-320 g). Sizing them to Falco's own loads might save 100-150 g (estimate; no flown loads exist to check it): AR 3.5 would sit near 1.08 kg, WL 25.7, still above Larus v20's 23.5 and on a pack that lasts about 8 min.

A servo regulator (for example the flight controller's own Vx BEC with its published rating, which the round-10 rule set does not model) would let a 3S pack and 13-16 g servos in: about -60 g on servos and +50 g on the pack; not enough for M1/M5 at these wing loadings.

M5 approach law (observation, not explored): runM5 approaches at the least-sink glide speed (Larus v20: 9.5 m/s) although the glide table reaches 7 m/s with 3.6% of the span stalled; and when design.landing.Vapp is given, runM5 still takes the pitch feed-forward from the least-sink row, not from the row at Vapp. A slower approach is a flight-controller choice that would act on Larus's 0.76 m/s M5 shortfall; it was not tried, because it is a new controller law that the orchestrator should rule on first.

rows.finding: failed after the refit (mean vertical force / weight 1.054). Diagnosis (subagent, scratchpad r11/diag-loop/): the round-2 test article is statically unstable in pitch (CG 2.8 cm behind the neutral point, static margin -11% of the root chord); buildControl's pitch law assumes a stable airframe, so the article tumbled (pitch +-80 deg, -26 m in 12 s) under the old fit as well and had passed by chance.
rows.change: test setup only: battery at x 0.30 m (static margin +12.6%), averaging over 40-50 s once the speed loop has settled, and a new assertion that the window is steady level flight (FLIGHT_TRIM_TOL climb and speed, pitch band under 10 deg). The 5% Newton tolerance and every other assertion are unchanged. Now: force/weight 0.981, climb +0.02 m/s, pitch band 2.1 deg. Under the old fit the patched test fails its new level-flight guard (descends 0.5 m/s, envelope-limited).
